key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation and ANN surrogate model can accurately predict friction stir welding behavior in HDPE and identify process windows that minimize defects.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers select rotation speed, traverse speed, and preheating conditions to reduce wormholes, stabilize axial force, and improve weld quality in thermoplastics.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of FSW in HDPE
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and force data
Process-map generation across rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL results matched experiments for temperature, force, and void formation trends.
watch_item: The ANN and process maps are based on the tested parameter space, so performance may drop when extrapolating to different materials, tool designs, or wider operating ranges.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
